chunks: Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, and Ibn Bukayr, from Lays Al-Muradi, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the wergild (blood money) of the Christian, the Jew, and the Magian. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Their wergilds are all the same – eight hundred dirhams, eight hundred dirhams.'

key_terms.دِيَة: Blood money or compensation for killing/injury

ai.seo_question: What is the blood money (diyah) for Christians, Jews, and Magians according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the specific blood money (diyah) for Ahl al-Kitab (Christians, Jews, and Zoroastrians) as eight hundred dirhams, emphasizing their jurisprudential equality in this compensation. It reflects the early Shia juristic consensus on the status of non-Muslims under Islamic rule, distinguishing their financial liability from that of Muslims while affirming their protected status (dhimmi). The repetition of 'eight hundred dirhams' underscores the definitive nature of this ruling in the Imami legal tradition.
